industry.structure: Fragmented mix of MNCs (Bayer, BASF, Syngenta, Corteva, FMC, Sumitomo), large Indian integrated players (UPL, PI, Coromandel, Rallis, Dhanuka) and many generic formulators. Generic molecules earn ~8-10% margin vs 15-20% for recently off-patent molecules; branded/differentiated formulations expected to grow 11-12% a year in India FY25-30. India is the 4th largest producer and 3rd largest exporter of crop-protection chemicals.
industry.chinaAndPricing: China is >40% of global chemical production. CY22-24 global destocking; glyphosate still ~70% below peak and Chinese supply an overhang (I-Sec, Apr-2026). SCIL saw ~10% adverse pricing in FY25 (volume +20%). In Mar-Jun 2026 the Gulf conflict and Chinese export curbs lifted input costs 10-25% by product; prices corrected from June 2026 as costs normalised.
industry.biologicals: Global biological crop protection seen growing from ~USD 8 bn (2023) to >USD 15 bn by 2029 (~20% of crop protection). Biologicals ~4-5% of business in India and globally (SCIL mgmt); SCIL at 8-10%. Indian biostimulant sales were disrupted roughly Jun-Dec 2025 by the new registration regime; approvals came Nov-Dec 2025.

regulation.status: Draft released for comments (deadline 2-Feb-2026) to replace the Insecticides Act 1968; earlier drafts of 2008, 2018 and 2020 lapsed; critics say limited change from 2020 draft, no clear criminal liability; states may impose temporary bans of up to 1 year

Draft nationwide ban issued July 2026 under Section 27 of Insecticides Act (expert committee cited poisonings, no antidote); SCIL management called it 'recently banned' and sees larger glyphosate opportunity

Oct-2022 notification restricting use to pest-control operators challenged in Delhi High Court; government said it will not implement until petitions are decided. Glyphosate is ~11-15% of SCIL revenue.
Flagged in AR 2019-20 as a serious threat to generic products; outcome not tracked in this pass
New regulatory framework halted sales of unapproved bio products ~Jun-Dec 2025 (hit SCIL and Barrix PGR/bio sales); approvals now largely in place

monsoon2026.facts: June rainfall ~35-40% below normal; season (Jun-Sep) ~12-13% below normal, weakest since 2015; drought in several states; kharif acreage ~1.5-2% below normal (rice ~4% lower); reservoirs ~71% of capacity; El Nino extending into H2FY27. Sector previews expected revenue declines of up to ~12% for listed agrochem companies in Q2FY27, with high-cost inventory and dealer stock overhang.
monsoon2026.monsoonDependence: ~55% of net sown area irrigated (SCIL mgmt); kharif (Q1-Q2) is ~60% of SCIL revenue

street.summary: Coverage is thin: only three houses have public 2025-26 notes - ICICI Securities (institutional), ICICI Direct (ICICI Securities' retail research arm) and Anand Rathi. All are BUY. Every disclosed method is P/E on FY28E EPS (36x-45x); ICICI Securities' initiation blended 36.5x FY28E P/E with 29.3x FY28E EV/EBITDA and a PEG check. Live targets range Rs 485 (ICICI Securities, cut 28-Oct-2026) to Rs 650 (Anand Rathi, 20-Jul-2026); S&P-polled consensus average ~Rs 584 (9 analysts) and Trendlyne ~Rs 586, both stale vs the Rs 336 price.

moat.evidence: Exclusive Indian rights to SCC innovator molecules under SCC brands, historically royalty-free (3% royalty now only on 2 products); specialty ~28-30% of revenue; Excalia Max and Lentigo launched FY26 (Excalia Max +50% in H1FY27); India elevated to SCC's tier-1 early-trial group with 2 molecules in trials; 1-2 new specialty molecules a year expected. Weakness: SCC controls timing and can redirect (e.g., AND exit and re-entry; Japan over-stocking).

15,000+ distributors, ~40,000 dealers, 60 depots across 26 states, ~600 sales managers and 1,500+ field officers; CRISIL: coverage ~85% of India; dual (SCIL + Excel) brand portfolio at all price points

R&D spend Rs 14.4 cr = 0.45% of turnover (FY26); 75+ scientists, 25+ patents; product innovation depends on SCC rather than in-house discovery

critiques.point: Growth is weak: domestic sales CAGR was low single digit FY22-25 and below peers; management admits peers grew faster and prioritises margin over top line. Standalone domestic sales were lower in FY26 (Rs 2,485 cr) than FY23 (Rs 2,607 cr); 5-year sales CAGR ~3-4%.

critiques.point: The valuation premium rests on optionality (semiconductor chemicals, CDMO) that may never sit in the listed company: the Tata MoU was signed by the parent, and SCC holds its global semiconductor businesses through wholly owned subsidiaries; SCIL may only earn rent.
